name: Rape and sexual assault
summary: Any sexual act without free consent. You can report at any police station, get free medical treatment at any hospital, and your identity must be kept confidential.
evidence: Seek medical care as soon as you can; any hospital must treat you free
If possible, keep the clothes you wore in a paper bag (not plastic)
Write down what you remember: date, time, place, the person, anyone you told
Messages, calls or photos related to the incident
Names of anyone who saw you before or after
documents: Any ID proof (Aadhaar, voter ID, college ID)
Medical / MLC report from the hospital
Copy of the FIR (you are entitled to a free copy)
first_steps: If you are hurt or in danger, call 112 or go to the nearest hospital; every hospital must treat you free (BNSS 397)
If possible, don't bathe or wash clothes before the medical exam; keep the clothes in a paper bag
You can give your statement to a woman police officer, and it can be recorded at your home
Call 181 or visit a Sakhi One Stop Centre for medical, legal and counselling help in one place
questions: Are you safe right now, and do you need medical care?
When did this happen (today, this week, or earlier)?
Do you know the person, or was it a stranger?

name: Sexual harassment and molestation
summary: Unwelcome touching, groping, sexual remarks, gestures or showing sexual content. In public places, on transport or anywhere else.
evidence: Date, time, exact place and route (bus number, train, shop)
Description of the person
Names or numbers of witnesses
CCTV locations nearby (ask police to secure footage quickly)
Photos or video if safely taken
documents: Ticket or travel proof if on transport
first_steps: Write down the date, time, exact place and route (bus or train number) while you remember
Ask the police to secure CCTV footage quickly; it is often deleted within days
Note any witnesses' names or numbers
You can file at any police station; in public places you can also call Pink Patrol 1515
questions: Where did this happen (bus, street, shop, college, online)?
Do you know the person or can you describe them?
Were there witnesses or CCTV nearby?

name: Stalking
summary: Someone repeatedly follows you, contacts you after you said no, or monitors your phone, email or social media.
evidence: A dated log of every incident
Screenshots of calls and messages showing number/profile and time
Proof you told them to stop
Photos of the person or vehicle if safe
Witnesses
documents: Call records (you can request from your telecom provider)
first_steps: Keep a dated log of every time he follows or contacts you
Screenshot calls and messages showing the number/profile and time; don't delete anything
Tell him clearly once, in writing, to stop, and keep that message as proof
Share your live location with a trusted person when you travel
questions: Is he following you in person, online, or both?
How long has this been going on?
Have you told him to stop, and has he threatened you?

name: Online harassment and cyberstalking
summary: Abusive messages, threats, fake profiles, hacking or monitoring your accounts online.
evidence: Screenshots showing the profile URL, username, message and date-time
Profile links (copy the URL)
Do not delete chats; export them if possible
Report the profile on the platform and screenshot the report
Keep the device; electronic evidence needs a BSA Section 63 certificate
documents: BSA Section 63 certificate for electronic evidence (police can guide)
first_steps: Screenshot everything with the profile URL, username and date-time visible
Report the profile on the platform and screenshot your report
File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930
Turn on two-factor authentication and change your passwords if you think you were hacked
questions: Which platform is it on (Instagram, WhatsApp, Facebook, other)?
Is it a fake profile in your name, messages to you, or posts about you?
Do you know who is behind it?

name: Blackmail, sextortion and leaked or morphed images
summary: Someone threatens to share private or morphed images unless you pay or do something, or has already shared them.
evidence: Do NOT pay; it usually leads to more demands
Screenshot the threats with the profile/number and date-time
Save links where images were posted
Do not delete the conversation
Report the content to the platform for takedown and to StopNCII.org
documents: Payment proof if you already paid
first_steps: Don't pay or send anything more; paying almost always leads to more demands
Screenshot the threats with the profile/number and date-time, and don't delete the chat
Report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930; women's complaints can be filed anonymously
Use StopNCII.org to block the images on major platforms, and ask the platform for removal (they must act within 24 hours)
questions: Has the image already been posted, or is he only threatening?
Is he demanding money, more photos, or something else?
Do you know him, or did you meet him online?

name: Hidden cameras and voyeurism
summary: Being secretly watched, photographed or filmed in a private situation, or such images being shared.
evidence: Note the location and time
Do not touch a hidden device; photograph it and inform police
Links if images were shared
first_steps: Don't touch a suspected hidden camera; photograph it and inform the police
Note the exact location and time
If images were shared, save the links and report them to the platform
questions: Where was the camera or recording (hostel, changing room, home)?
Have the images been shared anywhere?

name: Domestic violence
summary: Physical, sexual, verbal, emotional or economic abuse by a husband, partner or family member you live or lived with.
evidence: Photos of injuries and damaged property
Medical records of any treatment
A dated diary of incidents
Messages, voice notes or call recordings of threats
Names of neighbours or relatives who know
documents: Marriage certificate or proof of relationship
Proof of shared household (ration card, rent agreement, bills)
Bank statements if money is withheld
first_steps: If you are hurt, get medical treatment and keep the records
Photograph injuries and damage, and keep a dated diary of incidents
Contact the Protection Officer or a Sakhi One Stop Centre; they can help you get a protection order and the right to stay in your home
You can do both: a civil case under the DV Act and a police complaint under BNS 85
questions: Are you safe at home right now, and do you have somewhere safe to go?
Who is hurting you (husband, in-laws, other family)?
Do you want to stay in the home, leave, or are you unsure?

name: Dowry harassment
summary: Demands for money, gold or property from you or your family in connection with marriage, and harassment for not meeting them.
evidence: List of gifts, gold and money given, with dates
Wedding photos showing gifts
Messages or recordings of demands
Bank transfers
documents: Bills or receipts for jewellery and gifts (stridhan list)
first_steps: Write a list of all gifts, gold and money given, with dates
Save messages or recordings where dowry was demanded
Keep wedding photos and bills for jewellery (your stridhan belongs to you)
Approach the police (BNS 85) and/or the Protection Officer (DV Act)
questions: What exactly are they demanding, and since when?
Have they hurt you or threatened you over it?

name: Sexual harassment at work or college
summary: Sexual harassment by a boss, colleague, client, teacher or anyone at your workplace or institution.
evidence: Emails, chats and messages
Dates and places of each incident
Names of colleagues who witnessed or you confided in
Any earlier complaints you made
documents: Appointment letter or proof of employment / enrolment
Copy of your organisation's POSH policy if available
first_steps: Write down each incident with date, place and what was said or done
Save emails and chats; forward copies to your personal email
File a written complaint with your Internal Committee, generally within 3 months
If there is no Internal Committee, go to the district Local Committee; you can also file a police complaint
questions: Is it at a workplace or a college?
Is the person your boss, a colleague, a teacher or a client?
Does your organisation have an Internal Committee (ICC)?

name: Acid attack
summary: Throwing or attempting to throw acid. Every hospital must give free immediate treatment.
evidence: Get to a hospital immediately; pour plenty of clean water on the area
Names of witnesses
Any earlier threats from the person
first_steps: Rinse the area with plenty of clean water for at least 20 minutes and go to a hospital immediately
Every hospital must give free treatment (BNSS 397)
You can claim compensation through the Legal Services Authority (BNSS 396)
questions: Have you received medical treatment?
Did the person threaten you before?

name: Sexual abuse of a girl under 18
summary: Any sexual act, touch or harassment involving someone under 18 is an offence under POCSO, regardless of consent.
evidence: Take the child to a doctor; treatment is free
Write down what the child said, in her words, without pressing for details
Do not confront the accused yourself
documents: Child's age proof (birth certificate / school record)
first_steps: Make sure the child is safe from the person
Call 1098 (Childline) or the police; reporting is mandatory under POCSO
Take the child to a doctor; treatment is free
Don't question the child repeatedly; write down what she said in her own words
questions: How old is the child, and is she safe now?
Is the person a family member, someone at school, or a stranger?

name: Threats and intimidation
summary: Threats to hurt you, your family, your reputation or property.
evidence: Screenshots or recordings of the threats
Dates and witnesses
first_steps: Save the threats (screenshots, recordings) with dates
If you feel in immediate danger, call 112
File a complaint at the police station; tell them exactly what was threatened
questions: What exactly did they threaten to do?
How do you know this person?
